decision_log_refs.summary: Ch6 tax allocation methodology verified: income-proportional method (T_w = taxes × W_p/PI) confirmed against HDARP Section 3.3 extraction (pages 63-65, NRYwp net royalty framework). P09 implementation correct. S604 = S601 + S602 + S603 + indirect taxes is the formula verified.

entries.content: T_w = S601 (personal income tax workers) + S602 (social insurance tax workers) + S603 (property tax workers) + indirect taxes (sales/excise taxes allocated to workers). The indirect tax component is allocated proportional to worker consumption share, estimated from worker income relative to total consumption expenditure.

Component series S601, S602, S603 provide three direct tax components. Sales and excise taxes from NIPA Table 3.1 (indirect business tax and nontax accruals) and Table 3.3. Worker consumption share derived from compensation data and personal consumption expenditure (NIPA Table 2.1).

Total worker tax burden as a ratio to employee compensation (T/EC) rose from approximately 0.18 in 1952 to 0.32 by 1989, a 78% increase. The growth was driven primarily by rising social insurance contributions and bracket creep in personal income taxes before indexation.

The key methodological divergence across studies is sales/excise tax treatment. AS2 includes sales and excise taxes in the worker tax burden; Tonak's original framework excludes them. This is the primary source of the AS2-Tonak correlation drop (r=0.611 vs Moos-Tonak r=0.876). Moos includes indirect taxes similarly to AS2.

The sales/excise tax inclusion is theoretically justified because workers bear these taxes through consumption. However, the allocation ratio (worker consumption / total consumption) is an approximation. Sensitivity analysis shows that excluding indirect taxes shifts NSW toward less negative values but does not change the qualitative finding of predominantly negative NSW.
T_w = S601 + S602 + S603 + (sales_excise_taxes × worker_consumption_share). Worker consumption share ≈ W / personal_consumption_expenditure, bounded [0,1].

[internal-decision-record] (2026-04-09): The income-proportional tax allocation (T_w = taxes × W_p/PI) is the formula that applies to all T60x components summed in S604. HDARP extraction of Section 3.3 (pages 63-65) documents the NRYwp net royalty framework: the total tax allocation to workers in S604 is the empirical implementation of that framework at the aggregate level. P09 methodology verified correct.

Our adjustment procedure involves two steps. First, we estimate the social benefit expenditures directed toward wage and salary earners by the state, the taxes paid by them, and the difference between the two, which is the net transfer (a positive number when benefits exceed taxes and negative in the opposite case). The true compensation of wage and salary earners is their apparent compensation plus the net transfer.
entries.source_ref: ST_1994, Section 5.9, page 137; HDARP chunk_16 lines 79-83
entries.context: Defines the T1 = total taxes on labor concept that S604 implements: sum of all worker-borne tax components, paired with B1 (benefits) to compute NSW = B1 - T1.

entries.content: Appendix N lists the detailed calculations of our social accounting of taxes and benefits. Figure 5.22 shows the resulting tax and benefit rates (relative to total employee compensation), and Figure 5.23 shows the corresponding net transfer rate for the United States from 1952 to 1985.
entries.source_ref: ST_1994, Section 5.9 (Empirical Results), page 141; HDARP chunk_16 line 117
entries.context: Anchors S604 (Total Tax Workers / T1) to Appendix N as the canonical source of the disaggregated tax components and confirms that T1/EC is the published benchmark series displayed in Figure 5.22.

entries.content: It is immediately evident that, for most of the postwar period, wage and salary earners paid more in taxes than they received in social benefit expenditures. As a result, the true rate of surplus value is generally higher than the apparent one (see Figure 5.24).
entries.source_ref: ST_1994, Section 5.9 key finding, page 141; HDARP chunk_16 lines 123-125
entries.context: Authors' headline empirical claim about NSW: T1 > B1 (i.e., S604 > S607 in our scheme) for most years 1952-85, hence negative net social wage. This is the substantive result S604 must replicate.

entries.content: T1 = Total taxes from labor 1964 = 76.2 billion dollars (Social insurance 30.1 + Personal income 36.4 + Other 2.8 + Motor vehicle 0.8 + Personal property 6.1).

entries.context: Authoritative 1964 aggregation: S604 = 76.2 = S602(30.1) + S601_components(36.4+2.8) + S603_components(0.8+6.1). Provides the direct numeric crosswalk for V03 validation of the S604 = S601 + S602 + S603 identity.

entries.content: Excluded taxes (not levied on workers - footnote 2): Corporate profit taxes; Indirect business taxes; Estate and gift taxes (only apply to highest income levels).
entries.source_ref: ST_1994, Appendix N footnote 2; KB chunk_38 lines 268-271

entries.content: Group I - Social security taxes (100% from workers): Employee contributions; Employer contributions (deducted before workers receive income); Net government receipts from lotteries (treated as direct tax - footnote 1).
entries.source_ref: ST_1994, Appendix N (Tax Classification, Group I); KB chunk_38 lines 257-260

entries.content: Group II - Personal taxes (workers' share = labor income/personal income): Personal income taxes (federal and state); Motor vehicle licenses; Property taxes (primarily on homes - adjusted for homeowners only); Other taxes and nontaxes.
entries.source_ref: ST_1994, Appendix N (Tax Classification, Group II); KB chunk_38 lines 262-266

methodology_summary: Total worker taxes sum personal income tax (S601), social insurance (S602), property tax (S603), and indirect sales/excise taxes allocated by worker consumption share. Tax/EC ratio rose 78% from 0.18 to 0.32 over 1952-1989. [internal-decision-record] confirms T_w = taxes × W_p/PI income-proportional allocation is the correct methodology.
known_issues: Sales/excise tax inclusion is the main methodological divergence from Tonak benchmark
Worker consumption share proxy is approximate
Tax bracket indexation (post-1985) changes the income tax growth dynamic
State-level tax variation not captured in national aggregates
